records.subj: Adult-use cannabis requirements carried by Policies and Procedures rather than adopted regulations
records.kind: agency policy and procedure (not a chapter 54 regulation)
records.auth: RERACA provisions authorizing the Commissioner to establish policies and procedures pending regulations
records.st: in effect as the agency’s stated position
records.prog: never converted into adopted regulations for the adult-use market
records.out: The adult-use testing and operating requirements sit in a policy document, not in the Regulations of Connecticut State Agencies.
records.note: This is why the October 2026 question matters: a policy is not a regulation, and the difference decides what survives a challenge.

records.d: 2012 (medical regulations as first adopted; text shown in brackets in PR2017-029)
records.prog: baseline
records.out: "For purposes of the microbiological test, a marijuana sample shall be deemed to have passed if it satisfies the standards set forth in Section 1111 of the United States Pharmacopeia"
records.note: DCP Chapter 54 rulemaking (2012) | USP <1111> numbers not reproduced here (paywalled; TIER 3 reproductions only).

records.prog: baseline; no retest or remediation pathway in the regulation text at any date
records.out: "If a sample of marijuana does not pass the microbiological, mycotoxin, heavy metal or pesticide chemical residue test ... the producer shall dispose of the entire batch from which the sample was taken"
records.note: DCP | CGS 21a-408w (from 2024-07-01) permits repeat testing/remediation; which governs medical after 2026-10-01 is L-0170.

records.subj: medical — Sampling; reporting of failures to DCP
records.prog: baseline
records.out: "(b) A producer shall make available each such batch at the production facility for a laboratory employee to select a random sample." ... "(g) The laboratory shall file with the department an electronic copy of each laboratory test result for any batch that does not pass ... at the same time that it transmits those results to the producer."
records.note: DCP | AltaSci COAs 2017-2023 print "Sample(s) tested were collected at the Customer's production facility from lot(s) as designated by the Customer" (5,323 of 5,507 AltaSci PDFs). Failure filings under (g) are not public: queued request L37-OR-01.

records.prog: baseline (unchanged 2018, 2022)
records.out: "a marijuana sample shall be deemed to have passed if it meets the following standards: Metal Natural Health Products Acceptable limits uG/KG BW/Day Arsenic <0.14 Cadmium <0.09 Lead <0.29 Mercury <0.29"
records.note: DCP | Limits are daily-intake figures (per kg body weight per day), not concentrations; a lab must assume an intake to apply them. AltaSci printed As <4.206, Cd <2.704, Hg/Pb <8.712 ug/g = exactly 30.04 x the regulation figures (STRONG INFERENCE: 60 kg body weight / ~2 g per day); its 2022-23 template printed the raw figures as "< 0.14 ug/Kg" etc. No DCP instruction on the conversion was found.

records.prog: mycotoxin method (LC-MS or ELISA) added 2022
records.out: "less than 20 micrograms per kilogram of each of ... aflatoxin B1, aflatoxin B2, aflatoxin G1, aflatoxin G2, and ochratoxin A" (2022 wording); pesticides: "the most stringent acceptable standard for a pesticide chemical residue in any food item as set forth in ... 40 CFR 180"
records.note: DCP |

records.prog: raw product moved from USP <1111> to USP <2023>
records.out: "a marijuana sample shall be deemed to have passed if it satisfies the standards set forth in Section 2023 of the United States Pharmacopeia for all raw products and Section 1111 of the United States Pharmacopeia for all dosage forms other than rawproduct"
records.note: DCP Chapter 54 rulemaking PR2017-029 | USP <2023> TYMC 10^3 for dried botanicals is from reproductions (TIER 3); DCP (2022-03-16) called 10^3 a misstatement.

records.kind: Reported private email approval (no published instrument)
records.auth: Reported private email approval (no published instrument)
records.prog: lab-specific criterion outside any published instrument
records.out: NOT HELD. Reported: DCP approved by email in August 2020 AltaSci's request to raise its yeast/mould passing level from 10,000 to 1,000,000 CFU/g, paired with Aspergillus testing.
records.note: AltaSci request; DCP Drug Control approval (reported) | Certificates: 10^6 TYMC printed 2020-08-31..2020-12-09 (no Aspergillus test printed on any of 83 window-A certificates) and 2021-07-20..2022-01-21 (all 114 print it). Emails queued L5 OR-01.

records.kind: Adult-use Policies & Procedures PR2021-036 ed.1, s.21a-XXX-(f)(1)
records.auth: Adult-use Policies & Procedures PR2021-036 ed.1, s.21a-XXX-(f)(1)
records.prog: first adult-use standard; Aspergillus non-detect for inhaled products
records.out: "shall be deemed satisfactory if it satisfies the standards set forth in Section 2023 of the United States Pharmacopeia for all raw products ... Additionally, if the cannabis is intended for inhalation, the sample shall be deemed satisfactory only upon an absence of the pathogenic Aspergillus species A. fumigatus, A. flavus, A. niger, and A. terreus."
records.note: DCP operational policy (CGS 21a-421j) |

records.prog: adult use uses concentration limits (ug/g); medical kept BW/day figures
records.out: "based on consumption levels of up to 10 grams per day: ... Cadmium <=0.2 / <=0.5; Arsenic <=0.2 / <=1.5; Lead <=0.5 / <=0.5; Mercury <=0.1 / <=3.0" (inhalation / not inhalation, ug/g)
records.note: DCP |

records.subj: adult use — Retest / remediation after failure
records.kind: PR2021-036 ed.1 (h) and successors to PR2023-029 (h)
records.auth: PR2021-036 ed.1 (h) and successors to PR2023-029 (h)
records.prog: two-laboratory confirmation required for any retest or remediation route
records.out: "(1) Retest and reanalyze the cannabis by having an employee from the same laboratory select another random sample from the same batch. If the sample yields satisfactory results ..., an employee from a different laboratory shall select a different random sample from the same batch for testing. If both samples yield satisfactory results ... the cannabis batch shall be permitted for sale ...; or (2) Remediate the cannabis batch, if a remediation plan ... is ... approved by the commissioner, ... If the sample yields satisfactory results ..., an employee from a different laboratory shall select a
records.note: DCP | From 2023-Q3 through 2024-Q3 Northeast Laboratories issued 100% of registry-linked certificates (T1); a "different laboratory" did not operate in the registry record (AltaSci last registration 2023-Q2; ACTL.0000005 issued 2024-09-13 per L20). Whether DCP waived the requirement (P&P (l)/(n) waiver power) is not established: queued L37-OR-03.

records.out: Numeric standard 10^5 TAMC / 10^5 TYMC with named non-detects (text held: runs/S4-ALTASCI-20260921 docs; LIMITS_IN_FORCE.csv)
records.note: DCP | Magnitude caveat C-217/C-373: write as yeast-and-mould figure; aerobic count unchanged.

records.subj: medical — Microbial limit; method; pathogens; Aspergillus
records.prog: USP <2023> -> 10^5; qPCR; named pathogen and Aspergillus non-detects; 180-day qPCR grace
records.out: "tested using a molecular method that is certified for identifying microbiological DNA and approved by the Association of Official Analytical Collaboration (AOAC) International and includes quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) ... deemed satisfactory if (A) E. coli, shiga toxin producing E. coli, L. monocytogenes, and salmonella spp. are not detected, (B) the total aerobic microbial count and total combined yeast and mold count are each equal to or less than 105 cfu/g or ml, and (C) the pathogenic Aspergillus species A. fumigatus, A. flavus, A. niger, and A. terreus are not detected."
records.note: DCP Chapter 54 (notice 2021-12-29; AG 2022-03-29; LRRC 2022-05-24) | Culture (CFU) and qPCR results are not interchangeable (A-112).

records.prog: adult use on plating while medical on qPCR (L-0112)
records.out: "tested using a validated plating method approved by the Association of Official Analytical Collaboration ..."
records.note: DCP |

records.prog: plating -> qPCR for adult use; COA validity 1 year -> 30 days
records.out: "Collaboration (AOAC) International, which includes quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR)"; results "valid for a period of [one year] thirty days"
records.note: DCP |

records.subj: adult use + medical products — Remediation disclosure
records.kind: DCP notice "Labeling Requirement for Processing Techniques and Solvents"
records.auth: DCP notice "Labeling Requirement for Processing Techniques and Solvents"
records.prog: clarifies that remediation is a processing technique to be disclosed
records.out: "Processing techniques include any pre-treatment performed proactively as part of a standard process or reactively as a means of remediating the product after a failed test. These should be brand-specific and clearly listed for the consumer."
records.note: DCP Drug Control Division |

records.subj: medical + adult use — Aspergillus; qPCR; retest; remediation
records.prog: statutory retest/remediation path with no second-laboratory confirmation
records.out: "(1) Repeat testing ... in a form and manner approved by the Department of Consumer Protection. If all repeated testing yields satisfactory results, the marijuana batch ... shall be released for sale; (2) If such cannabis establishment submits ... a remediation plan ... and the commissioner approves ..., remediate ... and repeat all testing"
records.note: General Law Committee substitute 2024-03-12 (C-242) |

records.subj: adult use + medical — Retest; sampling; Aspergillus viability; chromium; point-of-sale notice
records.prog: two-laboratory confirmation deleted (bracketed); final-package testing; chromium added
records.out: "the cannabis establishment shall comply with the retesting, remediation, and disposal provisions set forth in section 3 of public act 24-76 ... which retesting shall be evidenced by a certificate of analysis. [may: (1) Retest and reanalyze the cannabis by having an employee from the same cannabis testing laboratory select ...]"; Aspergillus "not detected as viable ... confirmed using a validated plating method"; Chromium <=0.6 / <=2.0 ug/g
records.note: DCP (conforming to P.A. 24-76) | Posted 2024-08-27, before ACTL.0000005 issued 2024-09-13 (per L20). Innocent explanation: conformity with CGS 21a-408w(d). The statute let DCP set "form and manner", so keeping a second-lab check remained open to DCP.

records.subj: adult use + medical retail — Remediation disclosure (signage)
records.prog: new
records.out: "May have undergone decontamination and/or remediation processes to improve product quality or meet testing standards, which processes for cannabis have not been thoroughly studied for potential health impacts."
records.note: DCP implementing P.A. 24-76 |

records.subj: adult use + medical — Label: testing date/result; remediation statement
records.prog: (9) statement new; (6) wording "satisfactory or failing result" dates from PR2021-036
records.out: "(6) A statement that the cannabis has been tested for microbiological contaminants, mycotoxins, heavy metals, pesticide residue, and residual solvents, as well as the date and the satisfactory or failing result of such testing; ... (9) ... This cannabis or cannabis product may have undergone one or more forms of decontamination or remediation."
records.note: DCP | May be on extended label, insert or static QR code.

records.prog: lab preliminary results go to CATS; establishment preliminary results kept by the establishment only
records.out: "A cannabis establishment may conduct preliminary testing on cannabis, prior to submitting cannabis for [receiving a] certificate of analysis testing, provided that the results of any such testing shall be maintained and produced in accordance with section 21a-421j-6"
records.note: DCP | Pre-screening before the certificate test is permitted; its results are not public.

records.subj: adult use + medical — Disclosure of original failure; COA uploads
records.prog: interprets 32(g)(6) to require disclosure of the original failure
records.out: "In the event that a product submitted for final COA testing fails and is later successfully remediated and/or retested, the original failure, including the date of the test, must be disclosed on the extended label." ... "Upon branding, please upload all associated COAs as a single pdf, including initial failed results."
records.note: DCP Drug Control Division |

records.subj: adult use + medical — Batch size; random sampling
records.prog: lab-selected sampling from the packaged batch
records.out: "A cannabis establishment shall make the entire cannabis batch in final packaging available for random sample selection by the cannabis testing laboratory employee"; raw batches <= 40 lb; samples >= 0.4% of batch and >= 20 g
records.note: DCP |

records.kind: P.A. 25-166 s.30 (as implemented by DCP notice 2025-09-26)
records.auth: P.A. 25-166 s.30 (as implemented by DCP notice 2025-09-26)
records.prog: new statutory signage
records.out: "Cannabis establishments may use processing techniques to reduce, remove or otherwise remediate mold and other harmful contaminants. The use of remediation techniques may have possible health risks. For a list of processing and remediation techniques used on a particular product, review the product's extended content label."
records.note: General Assembly |

records.subj: medical + adult use — Analytes, Aspergillus, qPCR removed from statute; 60-day clock; deemed-approved remediation plans
records.prog: statutory floor removed; standards now in DCP policy/regulation
records.out: "(a)(1) Each cannabis establishment shall submit ... cannabis samples ... in accordance with the laboratory testing standards established in the regulations adopted ... pursuant to section 21a-421j" ... "(3) If the cannabis samples ... fail ... not later than sixty days after the date of such failed laboratory testing: (A) Repeat the laboratory testing ...; (B) Submit ... a remediation plan ...; or (C) Dispose of the entire cannabis batch"
records.note: DCP agency bill SB 231 / HB 5350 (L-0179) | DCP policy PR2024-040 still requires Aspergillus/qPCR (C-186); L-0550 on missing 21a-421j regulations.

records.subj: medical + adult use — Remediation by ionizing radiation
records.prog: new
records.out: "remediation of cannabis flower or other cannabis plant material by way of one or more exposures to ionizing radiation for any cannabis flower or other cannabis plant material that fails any laboratory testing due to microbial contamination"
records.note: General Assembly |

records.out: Policies lose force on the earlier of final regulations or 1 July 2028 (C-180).
records.note: General Assembly |
